(D.3)

Concretely, if
{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}
has column heights
\lambda_{L1},\lambda_{L2},...
(i.e. the transposed Young diagram
\lambda_{L}^{T}
has row lengths
\lambda_{L1},\lambda_{L2},...
)
and similarly
{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}
has column heights
\lambda_{R1},\lambda_{R2},...
then the corresponding
U(2n)
Young diagram
{\underline{\lambda}}
has row lengths
\lambda_{1},...,\lambda_{2n}
given by

\displaystyle\lambda_{i}

\displaystyle=k+\gamma-\lambda_{L(n+1-i)}\,,\qquad

\displaystyle i=1,..,n\,,

(D.4)

\displaystyle\lambda_{i+n}

\displaystyle=k+\lambda_{R(i)}\,,\qquad

\displaystyle i=1,..,n\,,

where
k
is arbitrary.
Given a charge
\gamma
and left and right Young diagrams
{\underline{\lambda}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}
whose widths are
\leq n
and whose combined height is
\leq\gamma
, this map gives a unique
U(2n)
Young diagram (one can add an arbitrary number
k
of full columns of height
2n
to this without altering the
U(2n)
rep).

As usual, there is an additional subtlety when taking the unit determinant constraint
U(2n)\mapsto SU(2n)
.
Indeed, in this case, the inverse map from the
SU(2n)
Young diagram to the operator is not unique. In particular there is freedom to choose the values of
k,\gamma
within a certain range

\displaystyle\gamma_{1}+\gamma_{2}

\displaystyle\geq\gamma\geq\lambda_{1}-k\,,\qquad 0\leq k\leq\lambda_{2n}\ .

(D.5)

After they are fixed, the left and right Young diagrams,
\lambda_{Li}
,
\lambda_{Ri}
, are then fixed by (
D.4
).
This non uniqueness simply reflects the fact that the operator itself is not uniquely labelled. Rather the following operators all correspond to the same representation

\mathcal{O}^{\gamma}_{\lambda_{L},\lambda_{R}}\sim\mathcal{O}^{\gamma+1}_{[n,\lambda_{L}],[\lambda_{R}]}\sim\mathcal{O}^{\gamma+1}_{[\lambda_{L}],[n,\lambda_{R}]}
(where by
[n,\lambda_{L}]
we mean the Young diagram with a row of length
n
appended above it).

D.3
4D
\mathcal{N}=2

This corresponds to
(2,1)
analytic superspace associated with the symmetry group
SL(4|2)
.
The transformations under superspace rotations are now given by two
GL(2|1)
Young diagrams. The key difference from the non-supersymmetric case is that these diagrams can now include an arbitrarily long first column.

Four-dimensional
\mathcal{N}=2
superconformal representations obey symmetric unitarity bounds and shortening conditions for both
Q
and
\bar{Q}
. This symmetry, often referred to as
two-sidedness
is encoded by the two distinct
GL(2|1)
Young diagrams on the supercoset space. In particular, shortening conditions for
Q
are described by the left diagram, while those for
\bar{Q}
correspond to the right one.
Indeed the shortening conditions of the representation as a whole are entirely inherited from the corresponding shortening conditions of the finite-dimensional representations of
SL(2|1)
.
The
Q
and
\bar{Q}
shortening conditions in
[
80
]
are denoted as
B,A_{2},A_{1}
and
L
, where
B
denotes isolated reps (i.e. there are no nearby unitary reps as one varies the dimension),
L
long reps, and
A
short reps at the threshold of the unitarity bound (which occur with two types of shortening conditions).
They map to our notation is then as follows

B\leftrightarrow[0],\qquad A_{2}\leftrightarrow\Box,\qquad A_{1}\leftrightarrow[\lambda>1],\qquad L\leftrightarrow[\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},1^{\mu}],\qquad

(D.6)

where
1^{\mu}
denotes
\mu
rows of length
1
, so the first column of
L
has height
\mu+2
.
As in the non-supersymmetric cases, the length of each row is directly related to the spin
\ell
and
\bar{\ell}
.
The new arbitrarily long column is linked with the
SU(2)
part of the
R
-symmetry (
U(2)
) representation, whereas
the remaining
\mathbb{C}^{*}
charge is related to the difference in the number of boxes between left and right Young diagrams.

(2,1)
analytic superspace description of all 4D
\mathcal{N}=2
representations. The notation
\bullet_{L,R}\coloneq\bullet_{L}+\bullet_{R}
and
\delta\bullet=\bullet_{L}-\bullet_{R}

D.4
4D
\mathcal{N}=4

This corresponds to
(2,2)
analytic superspace and the symmetry group
SL(4|4)
.
As in the
\mathcal{N}=2
case, we have two-sided multiplets with
Q
and
\bar{Q}
shortening conditions, albeit they are now encoded by two
GL(2|2)
Young diagrams. These can now have two arbitrarily long columns describing the three Dynkin labels of the
SU(4)
R-symmetry representation (together with
\gamma
).
Note that
SL(2m|2n)
is not semi-simple when
m=n
, which means that representations are actually of
PSL(2m|2n)\coloneq SL(2m|2n)/\mathcal{Z}
where
\mathcal{Z}
is the centre.
This induces an additional degeneracy in the
GL(2|2)\times GL(2|2)
representations, which can be fixed by requiring that left and right Young diagrams have the same number of boxes.
As one may expect, this is analogous to the R-symmetry being
SU(4)
instead of
U(4)
. Indeed, recall from the previous section that in 4D
\mathcal{N}=2
, the
\mathbb{C}^{*}
charge
r
depended on the difference in the number of boxes between left and right diagrams.

The correspondence between
Q
and
\bar{Q}
shortening conditions and
GL(2|2)
Young diagrams is as follows

B\leftrightarrow[1^{\mu}],\quad A_{2}\leftrightarrow[2,1^{\mu}],\quad A_{1}\leftrightarrow[\lambda>2,1^{\mu}],\quad L\leftrightarrow[\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}>1,2^{\mu_{1}},1^{\mu_{2}}].

Appendix E
Differential bubble property

In this appendix we provide details on the general derivation of the bubble property (
4.2
) in the case where both weight-shifting operators are differential (
3.40
).
In particular, we want to show that the following vanishes

\displaystyle(\bar{\mathcal{D}}_{\mathcal{A}})^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}}_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}(\mathcal{D}^{\mathcal{A}})^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}}_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}

(E.1)

\displaystyle=c_{0}^{2}\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}\bigg(\bar{W}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}\mathcal{A}}+X^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{\ \mathcal{A}}\!\!\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j){\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}(i)}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{b}}}\bigg)\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}_{1,k}\bigg(W{}^{\mathcal{A}}_{\ {\mathfrak{a}}}-{\bar{X}}^{\mathcal{A}{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}}\!\!\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\!(k){\underline{\mu}}_{R}(l)}\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}}_{l}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\bigg).

We defined the indices
i,j,k,l
specifying the Young tableau by

\overline{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}(i)}={\underline{\lambda}}_{R}(1),\quad\overline{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}(k)}={\underline{\lambda}}_{L}(1),\quad\overline{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}(j)}={\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}(1),\quad\overline{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}(l)}={\underline{\lambda}}_{R}(1),

where
\overline{T}
is the Young tableau obtained by deleting the last box from
T
.
Clearly the term
\bar{W}W
vanishes but no other terms do so. Let us divide through by the overall normalisation
c_{0}^{2}
and expand the brackets to obtain

\begin{split}&-\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}\delta^{{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime},{\underline{\mu}}_{R}}\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}}_{l}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}+\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}X^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{\ \mathcal{A}}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}W^{\mathcal{A}}_{\ {\mathfrak{a}}}\\
&\quad-\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}X^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{\ \mathcal{A}}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}{\bar{X}}^{\mathcal{A}{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime},{\underline{\mu}}_{R}}\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\mu}}_{R}}_{l}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{b}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}.\end{split}

Then, the first term simplifies by orthogonality of Young projectors
\bar{\Pi}
(
B.5
), and the third term does so by
[p,{\bar{X}}]=-W
,
[p,W]=0
and
X{\bar{X}}=0,\ XW=1
, giving

\begin{split}&-\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}+\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\delta^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{{\mathfrak{c}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}\delta^{{\mathfrak{c}}}_{{\mathfrak{a}}}\\
&\quad+c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\delta^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{{\mathfrak{c}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}\delta^{{\mathfrak{c}}}_{{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\,.\end{split}

(E.2)

To proceed we need to understand and simplify various contractions of Young operators. We claim the following:

\displaystyle\delta^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{{\mathfrak{c}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}\delta^{{\mathfrak{c}}}_{{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{h_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}}\left(m-n+C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)}\right)\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}_{1}\,,

(E.3)

\displaystyle\delta^{{\mathfrak{b}}}_{{\mathfrak{c}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}_{j}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{b}}}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}\delta^{{\mathfrak{c}}}_{{\mathfrak{a}}}

\displaystyle=\frac{h_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}(m-n+C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)})}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}(C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)}-C_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\!(k)})}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\,,

where
h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}
is the product of hook lengths of
{\underline{\mu}}_{L}
. The RHS of both equations can be fixed up to normalisation by the orthogonality properties of Young projectors (
B.5
) and (
B.6
) .
The normalisation can be determined from the definition of the Hermitian Young projectors in terms of standard Young projectors (see 2.3.16 of
[
67
]
and theorem 6 of
[
93
]
).
The first follows straightforwardly, and the second one likely admits a similar proof, but we have instead verified it for sufficiently generic Young tableaux
{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}
,
{\underline{\mu}}_{L}
.
Now, noting the identity

c_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}=\frac{c_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}-c_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}}{C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)}-C_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\!(k)}},

(E.4)

together with (
E.3
), expression (
E.2
) simplifies to

\begin{split}&c_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime},{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{R}}\left(-1+\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}\frac{h_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}}+\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}\frac{h_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}}(m-n+C_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\!(k)})}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}(C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)}-C_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\!(k)})}\right)\bar{\Pi}^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{R}^{\prime}}_{1,i}\Pi^{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}_{1,k}p_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\,,\end{split}

(E.5)

which vanishes
due to the identities

\displaystyle\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}\frac{1}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}}=\frac{1}{h_{{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}}},\qquad\qquad\sum_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\in{\underline{\lambda}}_{L}^{\prime}\otimes\Box}\frac{1}{h_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}}(C_{{\underline{\mu}}_{L}\!(j)}-C_{{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}\!(k)})}=0\,.

(E.6)

The first of these is a well known identity (see 2.3.35 of
[
67
]
). The second we have checked in many cases but have not proven in general. E.g. for
{\underline{\lambda}}^{\prime}_{L}=[\lambda]
, then the second equation above reads

\frac{1}{(\lambda+1)!}-\frac{1}{\lambda}\frac{1}{(\lambda+1)\times(\lambda-1)!}=0.

(E.7)

Appendix F
Consistency checks in 1D and 4D

In this appendix we provide some explicit checks of our results from section
5
against known conformal blocks in 1 and 4 dimensions.

F.1
1 dimension

We can describe 1D CFTs by choosing
(m,n)=(1,0)
. In this case we have for the prefactor (
5.3
) and the conformal block
[
25
]

\displaystyle P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}

\displaystyle=x_{12}^{-\frac{\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}}{2}}x_{34}^{-\frac{\Delta_{3}+\Delta_{4}}{2}}\left(\frac{x_{24}}{x_{14}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}\Delta_{21}}\left(\frac{x_{14}}{x_{13}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}\Delta_{43}}\left(\frac{x_{13}x_{24}}{x_{12}x_{34}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}\gamma}\,,

(F.1)

\displaystyle F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)

\displaystyle=z^{\lambda}\,{}_{2}F_{1}\left(\lambda+\frac{1}{2}(\gamma+\Delta_{21}),\lambda+\frac{1}{2}(\gamma-\Delta_{43}),2\lambda+\gamma;z\right)\,.

There is some degeneracy in this description, as operators in 1D depend only on their scaling dimension

\Delta=\gamma+\lambda\,,

(F.2)

but we will keep both labels
\gamma
and
\lambda
here to connect with our more general results. Consequently, all that the weight-shifting operators do in 1D is to shift scaling dimensions.

Let us begin by testing the two weight-shifting operators defined in (
5.18
) that turn a scalar block into a block with indices as in
\langle\mathcal{O}_{{\mathfrak{a}}}\mathcal{O}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\rangle
. For the first one we simply have

{\mathfrak{D}}^{[1]}_{{\mathfrak{a}}{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)=\frac{1}{x_{21}}P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)=-P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}+1,\Delta_{2}+1,\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)\,,

(F.3)

so it shifts up
\Delta_{1}
and
\Delta_{2}
as expected.
For the second operator we can use (
5.20
) and (
5.2.1
) to check that similarly

\displaystyle{\mathfrak{D}}^{[2]}_{{\mathfrak{a}}{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)

\displaystyle=P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}\frac{1}{x_{21}}\bigg(\frac{1}{4}\left(\left(\gamma-\Delta_{1}-\Delta_{2}\right)\left(2-\gamma-\Delta_{1}-\Delta_{2}\right)+\left(\gamma+\Delta_{21}\right)\left(\gamma-\Delta_{43}\right)z\right)

\displaystyle\quad+\frac{1}{2}\Big(\left(2\gamma+\Delta_{21}-\Delta_{43}+2\right)z^{2}-2\gamma z\Big)\partial_{z}+z^{2}(z-1)\partial_{z}^{2}\bigg)F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)

(F.4)

\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{4}(\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}-2\lambda-\gamma)(\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}+2\lambda+\gamma-2)P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}+1,\Delta_{2}+1,\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)\,.

We performed the analogous checks for both operators in (
5.34
) that create a block of the form
\langle\mathcal{O}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\rangle
,
finding that as expected

\displaystyle{\mathfrak{D}}^{[1]}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)\propto{\mathfrak{D}}^{[2]}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)\propto P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1}+2,\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,\lambda}_{\Delta_{21}-2,\Delta_{43}}\,.

(F.5)

Finally, we tested the internal shift operator in equations (
5.55
) to (
5.58
) by acting on
P^{\gamma}_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma,0}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z)
and confirming that the result is proportional to

P^{\gamma+1}_{\Delta_{1}+1,\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3}+1,\Delta_{4}}F^{\gamma+1,0}_{\Delta_{21}-1,\Delta_{43}-1}(z)\,.

(F.6)

F.2
4 dimensions

In four dimensions we can compare our weight-shifting operators to the comprehensive work and Mathematica package
[
15
]
.
We use the kinematic factor

\displaystyle P_{\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2},\gamma_{3},\gamma_{4}}

\displaystyle=(x^{2}_{12})^{-\frac{\gamma_{1}+\gamma_{2}}{2}}(x^{2}_{34})^{-\frac{\gamma_{3}+\gamma_{4}}{2}}\left(\frac{x^{2}_{24}}{x^{2}_{14}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}\gamma_{21}}\left(\frac{x^{2}_{14}}{x^{2}_{13}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}\gamma_{43}}\,,

(F.7)

and
F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\gamma_{21},\gamma_{43}}(z,\bar{z})
is the usual 4D conformal block, but for our checks it is enough to know that it is a function of
\gamma_{21}
,
\gamma_{43}
,
z
and
\bar{z}
. The
\gamma_{i}
’s are related to scaling dimensions and spins by

\gamma_{i}=\Delta_{i}-\frac{\ell_{i}+\bar{\ell}_{i}}{2}\,.

(F.8)

We begin again with the case
\langle\mathcal{O}_{{\mathfrak{a}}}\mathcal{O}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\rangle
.
By using the Mathematica package
[
15
]
we find the following two spinning conformal blocks

\displaystyle\Xi[I_{12}]P_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})={}

\displaystyle P_{\Delta_{1}-\frac{1}{2},\Delta_{2}-\frac{1}{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}\left(\frac{\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}}{z}-\frac{\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}}{\overline{z}}\right)F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})\,,

(F.9)

and

\displaystyle\Xi[\nabla_{21}]\Xi[D_{21}]\Xi[D_{12}]P_{\Delta_{1},\Delta_{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})

(F.10)

\displaystyle=P_{\Delta_{1}-\frac{1}{2},\Delta_{2}-\frac{1}{2},\Delta_{3},\Delta_{4}}\bigg(4\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}(z-1)z\partial_{z}^{2}-4\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}\left(\overline{z}-1\right)\overline{z}\partial_{\overline{z}}^{2}

\displaystyle+\frac{2\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}\left(2\left(z^{2}-\overline{z}\right)+\left(\Delta_{21}-\Delta_{43}\right)z\left(z-\overline{z}\right)\right)-4\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}(z-1)z}{z-\overline{z}}\partial_{z}

\displaystyle+\frac{2\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}\left(2(\overline{z}^{2}-z)+\left(\Delta_{21}-\Delta_{43}\right)\overline{z}\left(\overline{z}-z\right)\right)-4\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}\left(\overline{z}-1\right)\overline{z}}{z-\overline{z}}\partial_{\overline{z}}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Delta_{21}\left(\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}\left(\Delta_{21}-\Delta_{43}z-4\right)\overline{z}-\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}\left(\Delta_{21}-\Delta_{43}\overline{z}-4\right)z\right)}{z\overline{z}}\bigg)F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})\,.

Note that
\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}
and
\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}
are the two tensor structures in the conformal frame defined for this case in
[
15
]
. In order to write our tensor structures in the conformal frame, we have to set

\displaystyle x_{1}^{\mu}

\displaystyle=(0,0,0,0)\,,

(F.11)

\displaystyle x_{2}^{\mu}

\displaystyle=((\bar{z}-z)/2,0,0,(z+\bar{z})/2)\,,

\displaystyle x_{3}^{\mu}

\displaystyle=(0,0,0,1)\,,

\displaystyle x_{4}^{\mu}

\displaystyle=(0,0,0,\infty)\,,

and compute

(\overline{\xi}_{2},\overline{\eta}_{2})\cdot\hat{X}_{21}\cdot Z^{n}\cdot(\xi_{1},\eta_{1})^{T}=(\overline{\xi}_{2},\overline{\eta}_{2})\cdot\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{1}{\bar{z}}&0\\
0&\frac{1}{z}\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}\bar{z}^{n}&0\\
0&z^{n}\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}\xi_{1}\\
\eta_{1}\end{pmatrix}=\frac{z^{n}\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}}{z}-\frac{\bar{z}^{n}\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}}{\overline{z}}.

(F.12)

With this, we find that the first weight-shifting operator of (

(\xi_{1},\eta_{1})^{\mathfrak{a}}(\overline{\xi}_{2},\overline{\eta}_{2})^{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{D}}^{[1]}_{{\mathfrak{a}}{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}P_{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})=P_{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}}\left(\frac{\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{2}}{z}-\frac{\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{2}}{\overline{z}}\right)F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})\,.

(F.13)

For the second structure we insert (

\displaystyle(\xi_{1},\eta_{1})^{\mathfrak{a}}(\overline{\xi}_{2},\overline{\eta}_{2})^{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{D}}^{[2]}_{{\mathfrak{a}}{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}}P_{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})

(F.14)

\displaystyle=\left(\frac{1}{4}\Xi[\nabla_{21}]\Xi[D_{21}]\Xi[D_{12}]+\Delta_{1}(\Delta_{2}-2)\Xi[I_{12}]\right)P_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})\,.

For the case
\langle\mathcal{O}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\mathcal{O}\rangle

(\overline{\xi}_{1},\overline{\eta}_{1})\cdot Y_{1,24}\cdot Z^{n}\cdot(\xi_{1},\eta_{1})^{T}=-\frac{z^{n}\eta_{1}\overline{\eta}_{1}}{z}+\frac{\bar{z}^{n}\xi_{1}\overline{\xi}_{1}}{\overline{z}}\,,

and find that the first operator in (

\Xi[D_{12}]
from

(\overline{\xi}_{1},\overline{\eta}_{1})^{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}(\xi_{1},\eta_{1})^{\mathfrak{a}}{\mathfrak{D}}^{[1]}_{{\dot{\mathfrak{a}}}{\mathfrak{a}}}P_{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})=\frac{1}{2}\Xi[D_{12}]P_{\Delta_{1}\Delta_{2}\Delta_{3}\Delta_{4}}F^{\Delta,\ell,\bar{\ell}}_{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{43}}(z,\bar{z})\,.

(F.16)
